game_info.title: Dark Age of Camelot — Rules & Lore Database
game_info.description: Rules and lore for the Dark Age of Camelot module, based on the legendary MMORPG featuring persistent three-way Realm vs Realm vs Realm (RvRvR) warfare between Albion, Hibernia, and Midgard.
source_materials: Dark Age of Camelot MMORPG by Mythic Entertainment (2001-2018)
Dark Age of Camelot Official Website (darkageofcamelot.com)

rvr_combat.source: Dark Age of Camelot's Realm vs Realm vs Realm system
rvr_combat.description: The core combat system of DaOC — persistent three-way warfare between Albion, Hibernia, and Midgard for control of the Frontiers. Unlike traditional PvP, RvRvR means two realms can temporarily ally against the third, creating dynamic political gameplay.

keep_capture.description: Keeps are captured by standing inside the keep's capture point. The capture bar fills over time, affected by the number of towers controlled by each realm.
rules: Standing in a friendly keep does nothing — it's already yours
Standing in an enemy keep fills your capture bar
Enemy towers surrounding a keep speed up enemy capture
Capturing all towers around a keep makes it much faster to capture
Once captured, the keep switches to your realm's control
Capturing a keep grants Realm Points (RP) to all participants

tower_capture.description: Towers surround each keep and can be captured independently. Controlling towers gives a significant advantage in keep captures.
rules: Towers are captured by standing at the tower's capture point
Each keep has 2-4 towers (varies by keep)
More enemy towers = faster enemy capture of the keep
Capturing all towers around a keep is called 'towering out'
Towers provide elevated positions for archers and casters

relic_control.description: Each realm has two relics (Power and Strength) located in their frontier. Controlling your own relics provides realm bonuses. Capturing enemy relics provides even greater bonuses.
rules: Each realm has a Power Relic and a Strength Relic
Owning your own relics provides passive realm bonuses
Capturing an enemy relic denies their bonuses and grants you theirs
Relics are located in heavily defended keeps
Relic bonuses can be viewed on the realm war map

realm_points.description: Realm Points (RP) are the currency of RvR. They are earned through combat and objective completion, and spent on realm-wide upgrades.
earning: Killing enemy players in the Frontiers

champion_system.description: Players can become Champions by spending Champion Points, earned from RvR kills. Champions gain significant stat boosts and special abilities.
benefits: Champion auras that buff nearby allies

siegecraft.description: Siegecraft allows players to build siege equipment to assist in keep captures and defenses.

siege_tower.description: A large mobile tower that allows players to bypass walls and reach elevated capture points.
siege_tower.durability: Can be destroyed by enemy Tinderboxes

healing_tent.description: A tent that provides continuous healing to nearby allies.
healing_tent.durability: Can be destroyed by enemy Tinderboxes

buff_tent.description: A tent that provides stat buffs to nearby allies.
buff_tent.durability: Can be destroyed by enemy Tinderboxes

tinderbox.description: A throwable device that destroys enemy siege equipment.
tinderbox.usage: Thrown at enemy siege towers and tents

supply_crate.description: A resource needed to build siege equipment.
supply_crate.source: Dropped by mobs and found in the Frontiers

porting_rules.description: Porting to keeps and towers requires them to be under your realm's control.
rules: Can only port to keeps and towers your realm controls
Portal pad timer slows based on number of keeps owned
Porting from relic towns is disabled if key keeps are lost
Key keeps that restrict porting: Dun Ailinne, Dun Scathaig, Caer Renaris, Caer Hurbury, Fensalir Faste, Arvakr Faste
Ruined keeps can be ported to once all towers are captured

darkness_falls.description: Darkness Falls is the premier RvR dungeon, accessible only to the realm with the most frontier keeps. It features demonic enemies, sub-bosses, and the main boss Legion.
darkness_falls.entry_requirements: Realm must control more frontier keeps than either of the other two realms
mechanics: RvR combat is active inside the dungeon
Each realm has its own entrance wing
Exit portals near each boss send players to their home zone or portal keep
When portal control changes, the original realm can still stay until they release on death
Healers can keep players alive to maintain access after control changes

legion.name: Legion
legion.description: The demonic lord of Darkness Falls. Defeating Legion yields the best loot in the dungeon.
legion.location: Deep in the dungeon, past multiple sub-bosses

sub_bosses.description: Various demonic commanders that guard the paths to Legion. Each has an exit portal nearby.

labyrinth.description: The Labyrinth of the Minotaur is the largest RvR dungeon in DaOC history, located on Ellan Vannin Island. All three realms can access it simultaneously.
features: Three-way RvR dungeon — all realms fight simultaneously

class_balance.description: DaOC classes are balanced at the RvR level rather than in direct comparison to other realms' equivalent classes. Each realm's classes have unique strengths and weaknesses.
principles: Classes are very rigid with specific roles, play styles, and specialization point allocations
Each realm has unique classes that no other realm can access
The Mauler class is the only class shared across all three realms
Class balance is designed around RvR combat, not solo play
Specialization points determine a caster's spell path and effectiveness

stats.strength: Affects melee damage and carrying capacity
stats.dexterity: Affects attack bonus, spell bonus, and critical hit chance
stats.constitution: Affects health points and damage resistance
stats.magic: Affects spell damage, spell bonus, and mana points
stats.willpower: Affects spell resistance and healing effectiveness
stats.speed: Affects movement speed and attack speed
stats.luck: Affects critical hit chance and loot quality

specialization_system.description: Caster classes allocate Specialization Points (SP) to unlock and enhance spells. SP are earned through leveling and certain items.
rules: Each spell has a minimum SP requirement
Higher SP increases spell effectiveness
Different spell paths require different SP allocations
Some spells require specific SP thresholds to unlock
SP allocation is permanent and must be planned carefully
